visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A man with short hair and rectangular glasses, wearing a black button-up shirt, sits at a table with a grid pattern cloth in a dimly lit studio. He gestures emphatically with his hands while looking directly at the camera. Behind him, a warm yellow vertical tube light glows next to a wooden bookshelf. (2) A graphic of the Earth appears, sliced to reveal internal layers. The layers are color-coded: crust (brown), mantle (red), outer core (orange), and inner core (yellow). Labels in Traditional Chinese indicate the names of these layers. (3) The man returns to the screen, continuing his hand gestures. He leans forward slightly as he speaks. (4) A close-up meme clip of a green lizard wearing a suit is shown, followed by a sudden cut to a television color bar test pattern with a gray-scale block at the bottom. (5) A research paper title from 'Nature Geoscience' is displayed over a white background, followed by a split-screen animation showing the rotating Earth core. (6) A short clip of a scaly armadillo rolling into a protective ball on a dirt path is inserted as a visual metaphor. (7) An scientific illustration shows a cross-section of the Earth with arrows indicating the movement of helium-3 elements leaking from the core through the mantle. (8) Headshot photos of Professor Xu Han and a Japanese professor are shown briefly, followed by the abstract of a paper from 'Physical Review Letters'. (9) A meme animation of a sun with a human face (Nicolas Cage) rising over a field of green peas is shown. (10) A clip of Mark Zuckerberg speaking at a podium appears with a caption 'I was human'. (11) The man in the black shirt concludes his talk, pointing both index fingers downwards towards an invisible link area, maintaining a direct gaze.
